plate_findings.evidence: Multiple T2/FLAIR hyperintensities in the left occipital gray matter (a. FLAIR)

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: MRI shows multiple T2/FLAIR hyperintensities in the left occipital gray matter (Panel A), consistent with Alpers-Huttenlocher syndrome. B: MRI shows multiple T2/FLAIR hyperintensities in the left occipital gray matter (Panel B) on DWI, consistent with Alpers-Huttenlocher syndrome. C: MRI shows hyperintensities in the left precentral gyrus on FLAIR (Panel C), typical for AHS. Specific key not available in vocabulary. D: MRI shows hyperintensities in the left precentral gyrus on DWI (Panel D), typical for AHS. Specific key not available in vocabulary.

panels.figure_caption: MRI brain (left occipital gray matter and left precentral gyrus) MRI brain showed multiple T2/FLAIR hyperintensities in the left occipital gray matter (a. FLAIR, b. DWI) and in the left precentral gyrus (c. FLAIR, d. DWI) that are typical for AHS. FLAIR = fluid-attenuated inversion recovery; T2 = T2 weighted image MRI; DWI = diffusion-weighted imaging; AHS = Alpers-Huttenlocher syndrome.
in_text_mentions: with right-sided lateralization and worsening consciousness. Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) analysis revealed the progression of hyperproteinorrachia (protein 1.57 g/L). Serum analysis showed anemia (Hgb 87 g/L), and elevated aminotransferases (AST 1.2 ukat/L, ALT 0.6 ukat/L). Abdominal ultrasonography displayed normal findings. MRI revealed new multiple T2/FLAIR hyperintensities in the left occipital gray matter, bilateral basal ganglia, left precentral gyrus, and a stationary lesion in the left thalamus, along with an increase in the subarachnoidal spaces of the bilateral hemispheres (Figure 3).
